messages_body:
Hi Marcus —

Thanks for the quick intro call yesterday. As part of SilverLake Health's vendor diligence we need a detailed mapping and evidence package for your AI governance posture. Specifically we need: a mapping to NIST AI RMF functions and categories, a plain‑language note on how Redwood positions relative to the EU AI Act high‑risk obligations (data governance, documentation, human oversight), and a concrete regression/eval plan for model updates (sample size, pullback thresholds, and notification cadence).

Can you provide a draft by next Friday? Also, please attach any SOC2/pen test dates and a sample eval set (PII redacted) or a described format we can review.

Appreciate it — Dana
Dana Morales
Sr. Vendor Risk Manager, SilverLake Health
Hi Dana —

Thanks — happy to take this on. I've attached three artifacts that should address most of your asks: a NIST AI RMF mapping (Redwood_NIST_AI_RMF_Mapping_v1.3.pdf), a short EU AI Act positioning memo (EU-AI-Act-Positioning-Summary.docx), and our proposed Regression Test Plan tailored for SilverLake (Regression-Test-Plan-SilverLake.xlsx).

High level:
- NIST mapping: we enumerate functions (Govern, Map, Measure, Manage) and point to concrete controls in our platform (audit logs, model pinning, prefix cache controls, rollout policies).
- EU AI Act: we call out features that align to high‑risk obligations (documentation of training data provenance, KMS integrations, private deployment options for sensitive data). Where a legal determination is required we flag it — we do not provide legal advice.
- Regression plan: sample size guidance and automated drift/regression checks, with canary rollouts and three‑tier alerting. The spreadsheet contains sample thresholds and a sample anonymized prompt corpus.

Looping in Laura for procurement/contract redlines and Neha for controls verification. Monica — can you confirm the anonymized sample corpus location and whether we can share a small tarball?

Marcus
Marcus Lin
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference
Laura / Neha / Monica —

Quick internal plan before we send anything more formal to SilverLake:
1) Laura: confirm contract clause language around data residency and model provenance (we should confirm Private deployment option in writing + SLA notes).
2) Neha: please validate the mapping PDF against our latest control matrix (SOC2 section, audit log retention, KMS integration). Flag any gaps and note mitigations.
3) Monica: confirm the sample prompt corpus is fully anonymized (remove patient identifiers) and confirm location (secure GDrive folder) and access TTL. If we can provide a 250‑prompt sample, note format (CSV with columns: prompt_id, prompt_text, expected_metadata).

Goal: send updated package by EOD Thursday (2026-08-27) so SilverLake can review before their procurement meeting next week.

On the attachments: Regression-Test-Plan has a proposed notification cadence (48 hours to confirm a regression, then escalate after sequential failures). I've left placeholders for thresholds — Neha to advise.

Thanks — Marcus

Marcus —

Thanks for the quick turnaround and the artifacts; the package looks good at a glance and the level of detail in the NIST mapping is helpful. A few quick clarifications from our side after an internal read:

- For the EU AI Act memo: can you explicitly state which obligations you consider customers must own (e.g., labeling, explicit human oversight steps) versus what Redwood provides as platform features? That separation is important for our legal team.
- Regression plan: the Procurement team wants to see an example alert email and the timeframe for automatic rollback. The spreadsheet is close — can you add a sample SLO breach notification template?
- Attachments: we noted a reference to a SOC2 date in the mapping doc but couldn't find the attestation PDF. Can you attach the SOC2 report or let us know when the next audit completes?

Tariq (cc) will handle procurement sign‑offs — he asked we get a short executive summary for his committee (1 page).

If you can send the clarifications by COB Monday (2026-08-31) we'll be in good shape for Procurement review on Sept 2.

Appreciate it — Dana
